turns.query: We fill a bottle at the creek and read it on the bench meter back at the truck. How are we supposed to mix it before it goes into the little glass tube - is a good shake fine?

relevant.evidence:
Gently invert—do not shake—the sample 25 times (ASTM,
written commun., undated) to completely disperse the solids,
taking care not to entrain air bubbles.
relevant.locator: §6.7.3.A steps 1b-3e for samples below 40 turbidity units — "Gently invert—do not shake—the sample 25 times"

relevant.evidence:
invert the bottle 25 times using
a 1-second inversion cycle and pour off the sample
immediately to capture suspended particles.
relevant.locator: §6.7.3.A Preliminary steps and "For samples with turbidity less than 40 turbidity units" step 1 — "invert the bottle 25 times using a 1-second inversion cycle"

relevant.evidence:
gently re-invert
the cell 25 times and record at least three readings over a
short, defined time interval (for example, 30 seconds to
1 minute).
relevant.locator: §6.7.3.A step 4 and TECHNICAL NOTE (6) — "three or more sample values fall within ±10 percent"

relevant.evidence:
collect samples in
clean amber bottles, keep out of sunlight, and chill at or below
4°C to prevent biodegradation of solids or biological growth.
The holding time must not exceed 24 hours
relevant.locator: §6.7.3 Measurement introduction — "The holding time must not exceed 24 hours"
